channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajik and Spanish Scientists Discover New Geological Structures in Tajikistan
item.description: A joint geological expedition by scientists from Tajikistan and Spain, conducted from October 5-10, 2026, has discovered new folded structures in Quaternary deposits. The findings were made in the Khojasartez and Khojatanobchi diapiric structures area. This marks the first such field research in the region since Tajikistan's independence.

item.title: 10,971 Candidates Registered for Kazakhstan's Maslikhat Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan has registered 10,971 candidates for the upcoming maslikhat (local assembly) elections. Parties submitted 99 lists with 1,219 individuals, while 9,752 candidates are running in single-mandate districts. The Central Election Commission reported that women and youth constitute 43.2% of the party list candidates. Competition averages three candidates per mandate.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Pharmaceutical Exports Increased by 17.8% in 2025
item.description: Kazakhstan's pharmaceutical exports saw a 17.8% rise by the end of 2025, primarily to neighboring countries. The country also expanded investment cooperation in the sector, signing eight investment agreements totaling 391.3 billion tenge since December 2025. The first Kazakhstan-Afghanistan medical business forum was also held.

item.title: 56 Foreign Specialists Engaged in Surkhandarya Region Schools in Uzbekistan
item.description: Surkhandarya region in Uzbekistan has engaged 56 foreign specialists to enhance general secondary education quality and integrate international best practices. These educators conduct classes using modern methods and share expertise with local teachers, contributing to more effective and engaging lessons for students.

item.title: Arab League Demands International Probe into Torture of Gaza Detainees in Israeli Prison
item.description: The Arab League has called for an independent international investigation into alleged systematic torture and ill-treatment of Palestinian detainees from Gaza held at Israel's Ramla Prison. The league described the acts as crimes against humanity and violations of international humanitarian law, urging global action to protect detainees and end impunity.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Inspects Temirtau Tramway Revival Project
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the importance of reviving the tram service in Temirtau for the city's development. He noted that the tram is a significant link to the city's history and present. Tokayev also mentioned that residents are now supplied with natural gas and expressed satisfaction with the positive changes observed.

item.title: Uzbek President Aims for $50 Billion in Remittances Annually
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has set a goal to increase annual remittances from labor migrants to $50 billion. He stressed that current opportunities in labor migration are not being fully utilized and called for a fundamental review of state policy. Mirziyoyev believes this will improve family welfare and provide the country with specialists possessing international experience.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Results of Breast Cancer Screening Initiative
item.description: Kazakhstan has concluded a nationwide open-door day focused on early breast cancer detection. Over 2,100 women were screened, with 180 cases of pre-cancerous conditions and 54 suspected malignant tumors identified. All affected patients were referred for further examination. The initiative aimed to detect asymptomatic diseases early, emphasizing the importance of regular check-ups.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz Refuses to Disclose Contract Value for Gas Well Accident Repair
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has refused to disclose the contract value with China's CCDC for repairing the 'Independence of 25 Years' gas well accident in Boysun district, citing confidentiality. The company stated that multiple foreign companies, including those from the US, China, and Russia, were considered for the complex repair work. The accident involves high-sulfur gas emissions since September 2024.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise Norms for Establishing Psychological-Medical-Pedagogical Consultations
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to revise the standard for establishing psychological-medical-pedagogical consultations (PMPC), currently one per 50,000 children. The Ministry of Education proposes reducing this ratio to 40,000 children to expand access to specialized aid. This initiative is part of a broader interdepartmental plan to develop inclusive education from 2026–2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Raise Threshold for Mobile Transfer Tax Scrutiny
item.description: Kazakhstan will increase the threshold for tax control on mobile transfers from 1.02 million to 1.557 million tenge over three months. Banks will report to tax authorities if a person receives money from 100 or more different individuals in three consecutive months, with total receipts exceeding 360 monthly calculated indices. This applies to personal bank accounts not used for business.

item.title: Uzbekistan President: Foreign Work Experience Should Count Towards Pensions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that the work experience of Uzbek citizens working abroad must be taken into account, especially when calculating pensions upon their return to the homeland. This recognition is crucial for ensuring fair pension provisions for returning migrant workers.

item.title: Kazakh President Inspects Qarmet Steel Plant's Converter Workshop
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev visited Qarmet's converter workshop, a key steelmaking facility. He was shown the process of transforming pig iron into steel and subsequent stages. The company has invested over $2.7 billion in modernization and plans to produce 4 million tons of steel by 2026.

item.title: 3 MW Solar Power Plant Completed in Isfara, Tajikistan
item.description: A 3 MW solar photovoltaic power station has been completed in Isfara, Tajikistan, capable of powering up to 1,000 households. The project was funded by the government of the Republic of Korea and implemented by OAO "TGEM". The station covers 4 hectares and features 4,752 bifacial solar panels.

item.title: Second Amur Tiger Released into Kazakhstan's Ile-Balkhash Reserve
item.description: A male Amur tiger named Amur was released into the Ile-Balkhash State Nature Reserve in Kazakhstan, marking the second tiger reintroduced into the wild as part of a national program. This initiative aims to restore natural ecosystems after a 70-year absence of tigers in the region. A female tiger, Umyt, was released earlier.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 35.8 Billion Tenge for Maslikhat Deputy Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate 35.8 billion tenge for the upcoming maslikhat deputy elections scheduled for November 29. The Central Election Commission (CEC) confirmed the budget, which is comparable in scale to previous Kurultai elections. A significant portion will cover election commission member compensation.

item.title: Over 97,000 Kazakh Citizens Received Disability Benefits in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, 97,600 Kazakh citizens received disability benefits totaling 45.3 billion tenge. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that these payments are made throughout the period of disability until retirement age. Continued employment does not affect eligibility for these benefits.

item.title: Second Amur Tiger Released into the Wild in Kazakhstan as Reintroduction Program Continues
item.description: A male Amur tiger named Amur was released into its natural habitat on October 31 at the 'Ile-Balkhash' State Nature Reserve. This marks the second tiger reintroduced to Kazakhstan's wild, where tigers had not been seen for over 70 years. The program aims to restore natural ecosystems.

item.title: Kazakhstan's total state debt exceeds 41 trillion tenge, with loans from China up 2.7 times
item.description: Kazakhstan's total state and state-guaranteed debt reached 41.29 trillion tenge ($93.98 billion) as of October 1, 2026. The debt portfolio grew by 377.96 billion tenge in the third quarter of 2026. Loans from China increased significantly, rising 2.7 times.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Forum-2026 held in Munich, focusing on economic ties with Bavaria
item.description: The 'Uzbekistan-Forum-2026' took place in Munich, organized by Klett EDU GmbH with the support of the Uzbek Embassy. The forum discussed expanding economic cooperation between Uzbekistan and Bavaria, as well as professional education and labor migration. Participants exchanged views on potential partnerships.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Delegate Foreign Employment to Private Agencies by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to fully transfer the function of sending citizens abroad for work to private employment agencies by 2027. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced this, noting a threefold increase in agencies and a fivefold rise in citizens placed abroad since licensing reforms. The move aims to address issues like corruption and deception.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Views Qarmet Steel Plant's Converter Workshop
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev visited Qarmet's converter workshop, a key part of steel production. He was shown how molten iron is converted to steel. The workshop has undergone modernization, including new structures, to expand product range and increase steel output. Investments exceed $2.7 billion.

item.title: Ten Individuals Arrested in Atyrau on Suspicion of Extremism
item.description: National Security Committee forces, coordinated by prosecutors, arrested ten individuals in Atyrau, Kazakhstan. They are suspected of forming an extremist group and promoting terrorism and religious discord. Authorities seized firearms, drugs, and religious materials. Three clandestine educational centers for minors were shut down.

item.title: Almaty Experts Advise on Protecting Health from Winter Smog
item.description: Experts from the Almaty Air Initiative explain the health impacts of winter smog, particularly PM2.5 particles that penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream. Prolonged exposure is linked to increased risks of heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, and premature death. They emphasize that the body may not show clear signals, and the cumulative dose and individual vulnerability determine the consequences.

item.title: Second Amur Tiger Released into Kazakhstan's Wild
item.description: A male Amur tiger named Amur has been released into the wild at the Ile-Balkhash State Nature Reserve in Kazakhstan. He is the second tiger reintroduced as part of a reintroduction program, marking the return of tigers to the region after a 70-year absence. The tiger underwent veterinary checks and behavioral tests before release and is now equipped with a satellite collar for monitoring.

item.title: Over 9,000 Tajik Migrants Employed in Russia with Ministry Assistance
item.description: In the first ten months of 2026, 9,052 Tajik labor migrants secured permanent jobs in Russia through the assistance of the Ministry of Labor, Migration, and Employment's representative office. The office also helped recover 32.5 million rubles in unpaid wages. The representative office collaborates with Russian employers to expand legal employment opportunities for Tajik citizens.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Raw Material Race: Avoiding Resource Depletion
item.description: Kazakhstan faces a new race for raw materials, raising concerns about resource depletion. The article explores strategies to ensure the nation does not fall behind in this critical economic competition, focusing on sustainable resource management and economic diversification.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Electricity Market Challenges and Economic Viability
item.description: Kazakhstan's energy sector faces annual deficits, requiring expensive winter imports. Experts highlight the need for market reform to ensure economic viability. Analysis shows import prices significantly exceed export prices, indicating systemic issues within the electricity market.

item.title: Woman Arrested in West Kazakhstan for Allegedly Defrauding Residents in Education Services
item.description: A 35-year-old woman in the West Kazakhstan region is facing criminal charges for allegedly defrauding residents by promising various educational services. She is accused of taking money from individuals for help with university grants, qualification tests for teachers, master's programs, and diplomas, but failing to deliver.

item.title: UN OCHA Warns of Healthcare Access Crisis in Afghanistan Due to Funding Shortages
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that funding shortages are jeopardizing access to essential healthcare services in Afghanistan. Only 44% of the required $191 million has been secured, leading to reduced operations or closures of health facilities. Continued financial support is crucial.

item.title: Taliban Report 600 Migrants Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced the forced return of 600 migrants in 132 families to Afghanistan. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson, stated that returns occurred through Torkham, Silk Bridge, Islam Qala, and Spin Boldak border crossings. The figures detail families and individuals arriving via different routes.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Rides Tram in Temirtau
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev rode a tram in Temirtau during a working visit to the Karaganda region. He inspected the restored tram system, which was revived by Qarmet in 2024. Over one million passenger trips have been made since its resumption, with 30 km of tracks replaced and eight new trams acquired.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service Implements Automated Checks for Importer Reports
item.description: Starting November 1, Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service has launched an automated system for checking indirect tax reports from importers of specific goods from EAEU countries. The system verifies declarations for accuracy in product codes, units, and quantities, notifying taxpayers of errors before submission.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Digital System for Fair Coal Distribution
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Protection and Development of Competition is developing a digital system to control coal distribution, aiming to eliminate intermediaries and ensure fair access. The system will facilitate transparent and non-discriminatory sales of coal, particularly for communal and household use, addressing long-standing market issues.

item.title: Afghanistan Launches Polio Vaccination Campaign for 12.8 Million Children
item.description: Afghanistan has launched a nationwide polio vaccination campaign targeting 12.8 million children under five, amid a significant increase in confirmed cases this year. The campaign, running from November 2-5, aims to combat the disease, with additional regions having slightly different schedules. Children will also receive deworming tablets.

item.title: External Management Planned for Five Long-Term Construction Projects in Bishkek
item.description: Bishkek's Ministry of Construction plans to introduce external management for five problematic long-term construction projects in the capital and its suburbs. Minister Nurdin Oruntaev met with shareholders who have been waiting years for their apartments. The ministry will also consider involving investors and may approach law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Land worth 70.5 million soms returned to state near Bishkek
item.description: Land parcels valued at over 70.5 million soms, held privately for nearly 28 years, have been returned to the state in the Alamedin district of Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region. The prosecutor's office initiated the recovery of the 0.54-hectare pasture land, illegally transferred to private ownership in 1998.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan-Sharm El Sheikh Direct Flights Canceled for Winter Season Amidst New Egyptian Visa Rules
item.description: Direct flights between Bishkek and Sharm El Sheikh are canceled for the winter 2026-2027 season. This follows Egypt's stricter entry requirements for Kyrgyz citizens, including mandatory pre-arranged visas and specific travel conditions for those aged 16-40.

item.title: Ukraine President Zelensky Offers to Halt Attacks on Russian Refineries for Patriot Missiles
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Kyiv would cease attacks on Russian oil refineries if the US provides Patriot air defense missiles promptly. He mentioned ongoing discussions with US officials regarding this proposal. Zelensky emphasized that Ukraine cannot remain passive while Russia targets its energy infrastructure and kills its citizens.

item.title: UN Special Representative Emphasizes Journalist Safety as Crucial for Governance
item.description: Rabab Fatima, the UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Afghanistan, stressed the vital role of journalists in promoting dialogue, peace, and good governance. On the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists, she urged for measures to ensure their safety, highlighting the challenges faced by journalists since the Taliban's takeover.
